name: Sergei Parfenov
description: Sergei Parfenov is an AI/ML engineer and CTO in Barcelona. He builds AI products, evaluates agents and models, and writes about the engineering behind them.
summary: From a model to a working product.
intro: I build AI products and learning systems. I connect engineering with product decisions — from the first experiment to the backend and interface people rely on.
blogIntro: I write about AI engineering, experiments and things that break. Nearly 10k subscribers.
about: I’m an AI/ML engineer and CTO based in Barcelona. I work across the whole system: the model, the infrastructure behind it, and the interface people use.

I’m interested in what happens after the demo: an agent loses context, an API hits a limit, a convincing answer turns out to be wrong. I build evaluations and feedback loops to understand those failures and make the system more dependable.

My background is in software engineering and education. At Yandex Praktikum and TripleTen, I helped turn technical knowledge into courses, code checks and learning products. I connect the technical decisions to what people need from the product — and explain the trade-offs without asking everyone in the room to be an engineer.

currentRoles.description: Building a veterinary CRM for independent clinics — from the technical architecture to the product itself.
Building AI-powered learning experiences: personalisation, code verification and feedback that helps students keep making progress.

writing: I write about AI engineering: experiments, systems that break, and what the measurements actually tell us. My writing reaches nearly 10k subscribers.

collaboration.title: We could work together.
collaboration.description: An AI product to build, an agent to make reliable, or a learning experience to improve. These are the problems I like working on.
collaboration.approach: I start with a hypothesis and the smallest useful test. From there, I can build the system, coordinate the work and explain the trade-offs to the people making the decision.
collaboration.invitation: Tell me what you’re building, where you’re stuck and what a useful result would look like.

capabilities.name: An AI idea worth testing
capabilities.description: Turn an uncertain idea into a focused experiment. Build a working prototype, test the hypothesis and use what we learn to decide what deserves a full product — before committing to a big build.

capabilities.name: From prototype to product
capabilities.description: Connect the model, the data, a scalable backend and the interface. I can work across the implementation and help the team make decisions about quality, latency, cost and scope.

capabilities.name: Agents you can evaluate
capabilities.description: Find out why an agent fails, not just whether its answer looks plausible. Build checks around tool use, memory, retrieval and recovery, with traces you can inspect and tests you can repeat.

capabilities.name: Smaller models, measured trade-offs
capabilities.description: Explore distillation and fine-tuning for a narrow task. Compare the smaller model with a baseline on quality, speed and memory before deciding whether the trade is worth it.

capabilities.name: Learning, personalisation & retention
capabilities.description: Turn student needs into product decisions: where someone lacks confidence, needs more practice or gets stuck. Build the tracking, feedback and AI features around that — then connect the learning experience to retention.

projects.name: Screenshot model distillation
projects.description: A 7B-to-2B vision-model experiment, with a reproducible training and evaluation pipeline. A small proof of concept, including where the metrics misled me.

projects.name: Agent memory & provenance
projects.description: An experiment harness for measuring how memory compaction changes an agent’s decisions — including results that contradicted my own hypothesis.

experience.description: I’m responsible for the technical architecture and product engineering of a CRM for independent veterinary clinics.
I helped shape the AI-driven learning personalisation strategy and built features that improved student retention, backed by scalable backend systems.
highlights: On the Mastery Depth Tracker, I worked at the intersection of product and engineering: measuring learners’ confidence across skills and identifying where they needed more practice.

My work also includes evaluation, automated code verification, training hints and internal AI experiments. Earlier, I led the US QA Engineering course launch, with a 70% activation rate, and helped hundreds of students enter the field.
